title: French speaking HR Coordinator - Payroll and Operations
description:
FRENCH SELECTION (FS)

French speaking Payroll and Operations Administrator

Location: Manchester

Office based role

Salary: between £30,000 and £36,000 per annum depending on experience

Ref: 5520 F

To apply using our preferred format, please visit French Selection website, go to the vacancies page, search job reference: 5520 F

The company: A well-established international manufacturing business undergoing an exciting period of transformation and growth across its European operations

Main duties: This role would initially primarily involve managing UK payroll operations while providing HR coordination and administrative support across the business and its international locations - especially France

There will be opportunity for the role to evolve into broader responsibilities over time.

The role:
- Oversee the accurate processing of the monthly UK payroll and related payroll administration.
- Deliver efficient HR administrative support across employee documentation and HR processes
- Act as a key point of contact for employee and manager queries relating to HR and payroll matters
- Coordinate payroll information for smaller international locations
- Provide ongoing support to the French HR & Payroll team, including payroll cover when necessary
- Maintain HR records and reporting while contributing to continuous improvement initiatives and wider HR projects

The candidate:
- Previous experience managing UK payroll processes and payroll administration.
- Fluent French and English communication skills, both written and spoken.
- HR administration or HR coordination experience within a fast-paced environment
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills across all levels of a business
- Proactive and adaptable approach with an interest in developing broader HR and international payroll responsibilities.

The salary: between £30,000 and £36,000 per annum depending on experience

French Selection, leading UK-based consultancy specialising in the recruitment of bilingual and multilingual professionals for international business (industries and services). We are the leading recruitment consultancy for German, French, Italian and Spanish speaking positions. Also recruiting for positions with other languages such as Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Scandinavian languages, Mandarin, Japanese and Arabic.

title: Recruitment Officer
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Hays Human Resources are delighted to be supporting a highly respected, charitable organisation in Manchester to recruit a Recruitment Officer on a 12-month fixed-term contract.

The Opportunity

As Recruitment Officer, you will manage and coordinate the full recruitment life cycle, ensuring vacancies are filled efficiently, compliantly and with a strong focus on service delivery. Working closely with hiring managers and HR colleagues, you will provide expert recruitment support from vacancy approval through to onboarding and induction.

This role would suit a highly organised individual who enjoys building relationships, managing multiple priorities and delivering a first-class candidate experience.

Key Responsibilities:
- Coordinate end-to-end recruitment activity from vacancy advertising through to appointment.
- Review job descriptions and adverts to ensure compliance with legislation and recruitment best practice.
- Manage candidate and hiring manager queries throughout the recruitment process.
- Arrange and coordinate interviews, including preparing interview documentation and supporting interview panels.
- Conduct pre-employment checks including right-to-work verification, references and other onboarding requirements.
- Support the onboarding and induction process for new starters.
- Maintain accurate recruitment records and HR systems in line with GDPR requirements.
- Produce recruitment data, reports and statistics where required.
- Support continuous improvement initiatives across recruitment processes and candidate attraction activities.
- Promote vacancies through relevant recruitment channels, including social media platforms.

About You

To be successful in this position, you will demonstrate:
- Previous experience in a recruitment or HR recruitment-focused role, ideally coordinating recruitment campaigns from attraction through to onboarding.
- Knowledge of UK recruitment legislation, right-to-work requirements and pre-employment screening processes.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- A customer-focused approach with the ability to build effective stakeholder relationships.
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.

Desirable Experience
- CIPD Level 5 qualification or equivalent HR qualification.
- Experience working within an academic, research, healthcare, charity or not-for-profit environment.
- Experience using social media as a recruitment attraction tool.
- Experience producing recruitment reports and workforce data.

Benefits
- Generous annual leave entitlement of 32 days plus bank holidays.
- Enhanced pension provision.
- Employee assistance and wellbeing programmes.
- Training and professional development opportunities.
- 35-hour working week.
- Family-friendly policies and flexible working arrangements.
- Discount schemes and travel benefits, including cycle-to-work initiatives.
- A supportive, inclusive and collaborative working culture.

If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers. By applying for this job you accept the T&C's, Privacy Policy and Disclaimers which can be found at hays.co.uk

title: Senior People Services Administrator
company: Great Places Housing Association - Agency - Permanent
description:
You will deliver an effective and efficient People Services administration function to the People team and all Great Places colleagues, ensuring the accurate delivery of People processes across the employee lifecycle. You will act as the senior point of contact within the People Service Centre, providing quality assurance, supporting continuous improvement activities and supervising and developing a team of three People Services Administrators through day-to-day leadership, coaching and regular one-to-one (Great Conversation) meetings.

What you'll be doing
- Lead, supervise and develop a team of three People Services Administrators, ensuring workloads are effectively managed and service standards are achieved.
- Be the senior point of contact for People queries from colleagues and managers, resolving complex enquiries in a timely manner.
- Manage colleague lifecycle administration, including recruitment, onboarding, contractual changes, benefits administration and leavers.
- Conduct regular one-to-one meetings (Great Conversations), providing coaching, feedback and development support.
- Support performance management activities, helping colleagues achieve individual and team objectives.
- Provide a high level of customer service, contributing to a positive experience for all colleagues who interact with the People Service Centre.
- Process complex or sensitive administration activities and act as an escalation point for the team.
- Collate and review monthly payroll information including new starters, leavers and contractual amendments. .
- Review HR documents, ensuring accuracy, compliance and adherence to policy.
- Review work completed by People Services Administrators, providing guidance and support to maintain high standards.
- Coordinate onboarding administration, including new starter documentation, reference requests, right to work checks and DBS applications.
- Maintain People systems and records, ensuring data integrity, GDPR compliance and accurate payroll reporting.
- Monitor team workloads, priorities and service levels to ensure deadlines and service standards are achieved.
- Manage administration relating to colleague benefits, including WPA, The Marketplace, the Great Places Lottery and annual leave schemes.
- Support the delivery of People projects, audits and service improvement activities.
- Monitor and administer HR systems including Cascade, The Marketplace and Expenses+.
- Work closely with the Recruitment Team to ensure a seamless onboarding experience for new colleagues.
- Process People Team invoices, including raising purchase orders through the Finance system.
- Produce management information, service reports and data to support decision making and service improvements.
- Identify opportunities to improve processes, systems and ways of working within the People Service Centre.
- Assist with induction, training and mentoring of new team members.

What we need from you
- Experience of working within a HR or People Services administration environment.
- Experience of supervising or coordinating the work of others.
- Experience of using HR systems and maintaining accurate employee records.
- Experience of Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- A commitment to understand the challenges and opportunities that exist in the communities in which we work. We particularly value lived experience in social housing
- A passion to advocate on behalf of people and communities
- A commitment to work in partnership with others for the benefit of Great Places
- A commitment to continuous learning and improvement
- Ability to work flexibly and when needed

What you'll need
- Qualified to minimum GCSE Grade C/4 or equivalent in English and Maths.
- CIPD Level 3 qualified or working towards (desirable).
- Ability to organise and prioritise workloads for both yourself and others.
- A passion for customer service and continuous improvement.
- Ability to maintain confidentiality at all times.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
- Professional and value led with integrity, inclusivity and respect for diversity.
- Ability to coach and support colleagues to achieve high performance.
- Understanding of employment legislation, data protection and HR best practice.

What we give you in return for your hard work and commitment
- Pension DC scheme (up to 10% contribution from both colleagues and Great Places)
- WPA Healthcare scheme starts at no contribution level with £1250 of savings available per year (option to increase & add family members)
- Ways of Working We offer some hybrid and flexible working
- Annual leave Start at 26 days annual leave, increasing up to 30 days within 5 years + Bank Holidays
- Reward & Recognition You Count Rewards are individual reward's for going 'above & beyond'
- Professional fees The business pays the cost of one professional role related membership fee for each colleague
- The Market Place high street, restaurant & supermarket discounts, gym memberships, cycle to work, smart tech loans and much more
- Wage Stream You can access savings opportunities and early access to wages
- Health and Wellbeing Initiatives Our colleagues enjoy wellbeing campaigns throughout the year, with activities designed around our four pillars of wellbeing, these include career wellbeing, mental wellbeing, physical wellbeing and financial wellbeing

At Great Places we believe the wellbeing of our colleagues is vital to enable them to deliver to great services, all your benefits can be used inside and outside of work.
